definition: a person who seeks or is nominated for an office, prize, or position
hook: A candidate is someone dressed in white.
modernAnchor: A face on a campaign poster, a name on a ballot, a hand shaking yours at the door. We call that person a candidate.
journey: Latin candidus meant bright white, and candidatus meant dressed in white.
Romans who wanted public office wore togas rubbed with chalk until they gleamed, so crowds could pick them out.
The bleached toga announced the wearer was running, and a candidatus became anyone standing for election.
The chalk and the toga are long gone, but the word kept the job and dropped the outfit.
